title: The Secret of the Pipsqueaks
markdown:
The moon laid a pearl shard over Oakhaven School. Silas, whose errands collected small disasters, had been sent for Mrs. Gable’s trowel. Simple. A frisbee found his shoelaces. Geckos found the shed. Chattering found the allotments.

“Remarkable night sound,” he said, glasses catching dew. A picnic-rain shiver went down his spine.

Warm biscuit smell. Agnes, neighbour, basket brimming. “Heard a commotion. Determined. Shortbread?”

“Adequate occurrence,” Silas said, taking a biscuit he would not admit was perfect. The chattering organised itself.

Among the overgrown rows, bee-sized figures darted. Pipsqueaks: allotment guardians with worry too large for them.

“Humans,” one squeaked. “Clutter. Our reservoir is choked.”

They farmed morning dew in leaf channels. Wrappers and a plastic bottle had become garish mountains in the works.

“They don’t see us,” another sighed.

A third pointed. “Bartholomew is hoarding the best drops.”

A bristly badger puffed from a new burrow. The Pipsqueaks’ system was, in his view, messy. He was rerouting water to a superior larder.

“Mine,” he grunted. “For the good of the allotments. Can’t waste it on roots and petals.”

“Frivolous roots?” Silas blinked.

Agnes found a jam tart the size of a thumbnail. “Elderflower. Quite special.”

Bartholomew’s whiskers betrayed him. “Elderflower, you say?”

While he savoured, Silas saw a pearl-white button in moss, the sort that falls from a child’s coat. Peculiar, useful.

“Agnes. Small shiny things. Light-catchers.”

She dangled glittering beads toward the burrow, prize-collection bait. The badger shuffled. Pipsqueaks moved. Silas nudged a twig from a blocked path. A thimble became a scoop. Dew ran home. Tiny bells of cheering.

“Impressive,” Silas whispered, and his mouth almost admitted it.

Bartholomew, beads secured, grumbled for his dew. The Pipsqueaks had already gone, cistern full.

A biscuit, a tart, a lost button. In the days after, roses remembered how to be loud. Vegetables took themselves seriously. Students used the bins. The allotment, once an afterthought, breathed. Silas, polite, unlucky, impressed in a register only Agnes and the Pipsqueaks could hear, went to return the trowel, and did not mention the badger at all.
characters: Silas (polite but unlucky errand-runner who refuses to admit when they are impressed), Agnes (a neighbour who brings snacks to every crisis)
audience: teenagers aged 13-15, fantastic story for curious young teens
author: StoryGen Community
